priceSnapshot.note: changePct is measured against the last SETTLED UTC daily close (1Dutc bar ts 1786579200000 = 13 August, close 63,478.9): 62,874.9 / 63,478.9 - 1 = -0.9515%, rounded to -0.95. Against midnight's own 63,063.3 the session is -0.30%, which understates what happened in between. The important number is not the net change, it is the low. Midnight named 62,846.3 - the 13 August flush low - as the single line that would invalidate its 20 USDT spot tranche, and said the map beneath it was unmapped rather than empty. That line broke and it broke properly: the 09:00Z 1H bar SETTLED at 62,787.2, a clean 59.1 points through it, and the 08:00Z bar had already traded down to 62,685.7, which is 160.6 points below the line and the session low. Price has spent the four hours since building a shelf between 62,733.6 and 62,999.7 and now sits 189.2 points off that low and 28.6 points above the heaviest liquidation band of the morning. The bounce is real but it is a bounce inside a broken structure, not a repair.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $62,685.7 - today's session low, printed on the 08:00Z bar and the only price the market has defended since the 13 August floor gave way. Below it the measured map runs out fast: the liquidation window recorded $258,384 in the 62,600-62,699 band and NOTHING at all beneath 62,667, because price has not traded there. The next verified structure is 62,530.0, then the 6 August low at 62,457.1, then a genuine hole to 62,268.5. A settled close under 62,685.7 into that is the second reduce, and it should be taken without argument.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close back above $62,846.3 - the 13 August flush low that broke this morning - with aggregate BTC open interest NOT rising across the same bar. This is the eighth consecutive session the open-interest filter has been carried and it stays for the same reason: after a one-sided long flush the first leg back up is short covering, and covering does not hold levels. Note the gate is the broken level itself and not the 63,309.4 that midnight was still using. That is a deliberate step DOWN, and it is honest rather than accommodating: 63,309.4 stopped being the relevant line the moment a lower floor broke, and pretending otherwise would put the add trigger 434 points away where it can never fire.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from midnight's ADD to REDUCE, and this is the desk marking its own homework rather than changing its mind. Midnight bought a 20 USDT spot tranche at 63,063.3 and named 62,846.3 as the invalidation in the same breath. The 09:00Z 1H bar settled at 62,787.2. The invalidation fired. The rule the desk wrote for itself says the tranche comes off, and it comes off - a 20 percent trim of the spot book, roughly the size of what midnight added, sold into the bounce back toward the underside of the level that broke. Three things are worth stating plainly. FIRST, midnight's reasoning was not stupid and it is worth keeping the parts that held: it argued the 913-to-1 long-liquidation imbalance was forced selling completing, and it sized the tranche small precisely because every average was overhead. The sizing discipline is why this costs 0.06 USDT instead of a real wound. What it got wrong was direction of causation - a one-sided flush is not exhaustion when the level underneath it has not been tested, and this morning tested it. SECOND, the trim is NOT a directional short. The futures book stays flat and the swing operation stays WAIT, because opening leverage into a four-hour base 189 points off the low, with the 15m MACD histogram just crossed positive at +23.40, is the forced bad trade the desk keeps warning itself about. THIRD, what would make this wrong. The 62,700-62,900 corridor has now absorbed $2.05m of forced long selling in under four hours and has not broken; the 15m RSI has repaired from 24.63 at midnight to 41.02; and Brent, DXY and the 10-year are all quiet. If a 1H bar settles back above 62,846.3 without open interest rising, the reduce was a 190-point tax on being disciplined, and that is a price this desk should be willing to pay every time.

liquidityMagnet.note: WINDOW: 2026-08-14T08:05:31Z to 11:58:38Z, 200 fills, the freshest liquidation read this desk has had in a week - the newest fill is four minutes old. There is a gap between 06:58Z, where midnight's window ended, and 08:05Z, where this one begins; the API returns a fixed number of records and that hour fell off the end, so this window is additive but not contiguous. The finding is that the one-sidedness has gone from extreme to absolute: $2,565,680 of LONG liquidations against $6 of shorts, from a single 0.01-contract short fill at 62,919.9. Midnight measured 913 to 1. This window is effectively infinite to 1. Distribution: $1,148,559 at 62,800, $896,586 at 62,700, $262,158 at 62,900, $258,384 at 62,600. Pull is marked DOWN and the standing caveat still applies with full force - mass accumulates below precisely BECAUSE price fell through it, so it does not pull price by itself. The operational reading: 89.7% of all measured mass sits BELOW spot, the corridor from 62,600 to 62,899 has been comprehensively strip-mined, and there is no measured leverage left to flush between here and 62,530 except the 26 points above the session low. A break of 62,685.7 does not have a cushion of forced sellers to absorb it.

scalpContext.intradayBias: Bearish structure, basing tape - tradeable only at the edges and only small. Price has held a 314-point box between 62,685.7 and 62,999.7 for four hours after breaking the 13 August floor, and both edges are defined by real prints rather than indicators. The long edge is a reclaim of the 15m EMA20 at 62,932.90 with the 62,846.3 flip level as the backstop; the short edge is a loss of 62,685.7 into a corridor where the liquidation map goes blank below 62,667.0. Between those two the 15m RSI at 41.02 and the newly positive 15m histogram argue against pressing shorts, while the 1H MACD at -191.53 and every average overhead argue against pressing longs. That is a range, and ranges punish conviction.

calibration.note: Midnight's reduce line was 62,846.3 and it FIRED - the 09:00Z 1H bar settled 62,787.2, and the 08:00Z bar had already traded to 62,685.7. Midnight's own action is marked NO. It bought a 20 USDT spot tranche at 63,063.3 arguing that a 913-to-1 long-liquidation imbalance was forced selling completing; spot is 188.4 points lower, the tranche is down 0.30% or about 0.06 USDT, and the thesis was wrong in a specific and instructive way. Exhaustion is not measurable from the size of a flush alone - it needs a level underneath that holds when tested, and the level had not been tested when midnight bought. It was tested three hours later and it failed. The pattern the desk has been tracking for two weeks holds: LEVELS keep being right and TRADES keep being wrong, and the two sessions that scored YES were both sessions where the desk reduced into strength rather than adding into weakness. That is now three data points saying the same thing, and this session acts on it - the trim is the trade the record supports.
